This guide explains what CTET Basic Geometrical Ideas (2-D) actually tests, the facts worth memorising, the mistakes that quietly cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now to see where you stand.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CTET Paper 2 asks on Basic Geometrical Ideas (2-D)

Questions test the building blocks of geometry — points, lines, line segments, rays, angles — and the terms for polygons and circles (vertex, side, diagonal, radius, diameter, chord).

Key facts & formulas to remember

  • A line extends endlessly both ways; a ray has one endpoint; a segment has two.
  • Intersecting lines meet at a point; parallel lines never meet.
  • A polygon is a simple closed figure made of line segments.
  • A diagonal joins two non-adjacent vertices of a polygon.
  • In a circle: radius = centre to edge, diameter = 2 × radius, chord = any segment joining two points on the circle.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Confusing a line, a ray and a line segment.
  • Calling any closed curve a polygon (a polygon has straight sides only).
  • Mixing up chord, diameter and radius.

quiz.title: CTET Basic Geometrical Ideas (2-D) Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CTET Paper II–pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: CTET Paper 2 Maths: Basic Geometrical Ideas (2-D)

questions.q: How many lines can pass through a given single fixed point in a plane?
questions.explanation: An infinite number of lines can be drawn passing through a single given point in a plane, as rotation around that point creates countless trajectories.

questions.q: Which of the following 2-D geometric figures has a starting point but no end point, extending endlessly in one direction?
questions.explanation: A ray is a portion of a line that starts at a fixed point (origin) and goes on endlessly in one direction.

questions.q: If three or more points lie on the same straight line, what are they called?
questions.explanation: Points that lie on the same single straight line are termed collinear points. If they do not lie on the same line, they are non-collinear.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of line segments required to form a closed polygon?
questions.explanation: A polygon is a simple closed curve made up entirely of line segments. The simplest and polygon with the minimum number of sides is a triangle, which requires three line segments.

questions.q: Which of the following differentiates a regular polygon from an irregular polygon?
options: A regular polygon is equilateral and equiangular.
An irregular polygon cannot be a closed curve.
An irregular polygon always has curved boundaries.
A regular polygon must have an even number of sides.
questions.explanation: A regular polygon is defined as a polygon in which all sides are equal in length (equilateral) and all interior angles are equal in measure (equiangular).

questions.q: Consider a polygon with 7 sides (heptagon). What is the total number of diagonals that can be drawn inside this polygon?
questions.explanation: The number of diagonals in an n-sided polygon is given by the formula n(n-3)/2. For n = 7: 7(7-3)/2 = (7 imes 4)/2 = 14.

questions.q: If four distinct lines are drawn in a plane, what is the maximum possible number of points of intersection between them?
questions.explanation: The maximum number of intersection points for n lines in a plane is given by n(n-1)/2. For 4 lines: 4 imes 3 / 2 = 6 points.

questions.q: Which of the following represents an open curve?
options: The letter 'S' drawn in standard font
questions.explanation: An open curve is one that does not enclose an area and has two distinct endpoints (like the letter 'S'). Circles, triangles, and rectangles are closed curves.

questions.q: What is the interior region of a closed curve combined with its boundary known as?
questions.explanation: In geometry, the interior of a curve together with its boundary forms the closed region bounded by the curve.

questions.q: In a convex polygon, the sum of all interior angles is 1080^\^c^i^r^c. How many sides does this polygon have?
questions.explanation: The sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon is (n-2) imes 180^\^c^i^r^c. Given (n-2) imes 180^\^c^i^r^c = 1080^\^c^i^r^c, dividing by 180 gives n-2 = 6, so n = 8 (an octagon).

faq.q: What is the difference between a line and a line segment?
faq.a: A line has no endpoints and extends forever in both directions; a line segment is a part of a line with two definite endpoints.
No. A polygon is bounded by straight line segments; a circle has a curved boundary.
